content.title: Is Walmart open or closed on Easter? Here's what to know
content.text: April 5, 2026, 12:01 a.m. ETEaster has arrived, and whether you are hosting the holiday festivities at home or traveling to meet up with friends and family elsewhere, shoppers should have some options if they need to make a last-minute trip to the grocery store.Some restaurants, grocery stores, and national retailers will be closed on Sunday, April 5. Banks, post offices, shipping services, and the stock market will also be closed on Easter.Walmart will be an option for shoppers, as its store will remain open under regular hours on Easter. Most Walmart locations are open from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily.What grocery stores are open and closed on Easter?In addition to Walmart, here are the grocery stores that will be open on Easter. Hours are listed for the companies that provided them.Most stores in the Kroger family of companies will be open on Sunday (Baker’s, City Market, Dillons, Food 4 Less, Foods Co, Fred Meyer, Fry’s, Gerbes, Jay C Food Store, King Soopers, Kroger, Mariano’s, Metro Market, Pay-Less Super Markets, Pick’n Save, QFC, Ralphs, Ruler, Smith’s Food and Drug).BJ's Wholesale ClubTrader Joe'sFood LionWhole FoodsSafewayWegmansMeijer; 6 a.m. to midnightHarris TeeterMost Albertson's banner stores will be open on Easter (Safeway, Albertsons, Jewel-Osco, ACME, Vons and Tom Thumb).LidlGiant Eagle; Stores will close at 4 p.m.Winn-DixieThe following grocery stores are closed on Easter.CostcoSam's ClubTargetAldiPublixWhat retail stores are open and closed on Easter?Stores listed below will be open on April 5. Hours are listed for the companies that provided them.Home Depot; 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.Ace HardwareSephoraBarnes & NobleBass Pro Shop; 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.Cabela's; 10 a.m. to 7 p.m.REI; Noon to 6 p.m.IKEA stores will close at 6 p.m.PetcoPetSmart; 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.Tractor Supply Company; 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.Stores listed below will be closed on April 5.TargetTJ MaxxMarshall'sHomeGoodsLowe'sMacy'sKohl'sVictoria's SecretBelkOffice DepotOfficeMaxGabe Hauari is a national trending news reporter at USA TODAY.
